The model also learned the specific problem of finding the smallest number that requires 100 iterations of the sieve—determined to be 247—by recognizing that each prime elimination reduces the candidate pool and that the number of iterations corresponds to the number of primes less than or equal to N.

The training covers the problem's constraints—only one prisoner can enter the room at a time, prisoners cannot communicate, and the warden chooses prisoners randomly—alongside the solution mechanism: designating a 'counter' prisoner who toggles the bulb only when it's off, and others toggling it only when it's on. The model internalized the logical reasoning required to coordinate group knowledge under strict information constraints.
